texts.2d69495e9021:
Access to the data will enable the Local Authority to undertake locally-focused and locally-responsive analyses of health status and health outcomes. For example, the data will be used to produce analyses of health inequalities for non-standard geographies and for specific social or ethnic groups in the local population to help ensure that the health challenges facing the local population – particularly the most disadvantaged – have been identified and responded to appropriately by the Local Authority and its partners.

It is recognised that in fulfilling its public health duties using HES data, the Local Authority will deliver significant benefits.  The Local Authority therefore commits in any renewal request to providing additional detail on benefits that relate to their local use of the data.

texts.52e8593c4b73:
Feb 2021
Examples of how the Local Authority has used the HES data include:

~ looking at drug and alcohol misuse hospital admissions and A&E attendances to inform the statutory community safety needs assessment. This informs multi-agency action on community safety to improve lives and foster stronger communities by reducing crime, anti-social behaviour, alcohol misuse and supply, and the use and harm caused by drugs throughout the city. HES data on alcohol specific admissions, hospital admissions with a primary or secondary diagnosis of drug related mental  health and behavioural disorders and hospital admissions rate for poisoning by illicit drugs at electoral ward and IMD quintile highlights inequalities and geospatial differences at a sub city level

~ HES data has been used to examine falls in the city to inform for inclusion in models predicting demand for services and adult social care in Southampton looking at rate of admissions due to injury as result of a fall in people over 65 year. Informing commissioning decisions and service planning, reducing falls is a national public health target. 

~ HES data has also been used to analyse health inequalities in the city by deprivation quintile; this analysis has also enabled a better understanding of how the inequality gap over time has changed informing discussions about health resource allocation across the city. 

~ HES data has been used to analyse self-harm in the city by electoral deprivation quintile. These profiles have been used by the Suicide Prevention Programme Manager for Hampshire & IoW STP to inform strategic planning

~ HES data has been used to develop NHS locality and Primary Care Network (PCN) health profiles. These profiles have been used by clinicians and health professionals to set priorities and target action in their local areas.

~ HES data has been used extensively in the JSNA which has been instrumental in refreshing and monitoring the Health & Wellbeing Strategy for the City.
texts.5cf30126c6cf:
Access to the data will enable the Local Authority to undertake locally-focused and locally-responsive analyses of health status and health outcomes. For example, the data will be used to produce analyses of health inequalities for non-standard geographies and for specific social or ethnic groups in the local population to help ensure that the health challenges facing the local population – particularly the most disadvantaged – have been identified and responded to appropriately by the Local Authority and its partners.
It is recognised that in fulfilling its public health duties using HES data, the Local Authority will deliver significant benefits. Examples of how the Local Authority has used the HES data in the last 12 months include looking at drug and alcohol misuse hospital admissions and A&E attendances to inform a local needs assessment. This has allowed the LA to focus commissioned services on those areas and population groups most at risk of abuse. Hospital admissions for patients with Asthma, COPD and Cardiovascualr Disease has also been used to identify areas of high air pollution and the population groups most at risk from it's adverse affects to inform the development of a City Clean Air Strategy. In addition, HES data has been used extensively in the JSNA which has been instrumental in refreshing the Health & Wellbeing Strategy for the City.

~ HES data has been used to investigate alcohol specific and related admissions in the city and the drivers behind recent increases.
